name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Pancreas
aliases: Primary Squamous Cell Carcinoma of Pancreas

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Pancreatic Squamous Cell Carcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant squamous cells with keratinization and intercellular bridges on pancreatic tissue biopsy
Exclusion of squamous cell carcinoma originating from other primary sites (e.g., lung, esophagus) through imaging and clinical evaluation
Radiologic evidence of a pancreatic mass with features atypical for adenocarcinoma, such as central necrosis or cystic degeneration
Positive immunohistochemical staining for squamous markers (e.g., p40, CK5/6) and negative for adenocarcinoma markers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of squamous cell carcinoma in pancreatic tissue with exclusion of other primary squamous tumors
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma from other sites.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable abdominal mass in epigastric region
Progressive jaundice due to biliary obstruction

common.symptomName: Persistent upper abdominal pain radiating to the back
searchTerms: upper belly pain radiating to back
constant pain in upper stomach area
itchy skin due to liver problem
fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.symptomName: Early satiety due to mass effect
searchTerms: loss of appetite due to pressure
severe weight loss with muscle loss

laboratory: Elevated serum bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase indicating biliary obstruction
Mild anemia on complete blood count
Occasional hypercalcemia due to paraneoplastic syndrome
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT showing hypodense pancreatic mass with central necrosis
MRI demonstrating heterogeneous pancreatic lesion with cystic components
Endoscopic ultrasound-guided biopsy confirming tumor histology
genetic: Absence of KRAS mutations typical of pancreatic adenocarcinoma
other: Immunohistochemical positivity for p40 and CK5/6
Negative staining for adenocarcinoma markers such as CK7 and CK20

distinguishingFeatures: More common presentation with painless jaundice
History of primary squamous cell carcinoma elsewhere (e.g., lung, head and neck)
Clinical and radiologic evidence of primary tumor outside pancreas

redFlags: Severe unintentional weight loss and cachexia
references: Huang et al., Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Pancreas: A Clinicopathologic Study, Journal of Clinical Oncology, 2022
